item.title: Florida Counts Its Election Ballots Fast. Why Can’t California Keep Up?
item.description: Florida counted most of its primary ballots within hours on Tuesday night, well ahead of the days California took to report the results of its major election.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: Election workers sort vote-by-mail ballots at the Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Office for the Florida primary election in Doral, Fla., on Tuesday.

item.title: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s ‘Road Trip’ Highlights America, and Some of Its Sponsors
item.description: The transportation secretary’s six-part YouTube series is fueling ethical concerns over family adventures funded in large part by corporate sponsors regulated by his department.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian

item.media:description: The reality road trip series tracks Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, his wife, their nine children and his son-in-law.

item.title: Nancy Kissinger, Wife of Former Secretary of State, Dies at 92
item.description: A foreign policy specialist, she was politically savvy and well versed in global issues, and traveled widely with her husband, Henry A. Kissinger, on his diplomatic missions.
item.dc:creator: Robert D. McFadden
item.media:description: Nancy Kissinger, then Nancy Maginnes, with her future husband, Henry A. Kissinger, in Jerusalem in 1970. She was a fierce defender of Mr. Kissinger, a polarizing figure with a hotly disputed reputation.

item.title: Aisha Wahab Wins California Special Election to Replace Eric Swalwell
item.description: Aisha Wahab, a Democratic state senator in California, will fill out the term of Eric Swalwell, who resigned from the House amid accusations of sexual misconduct.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina
item.media:description: State Senator Aisha Wahab addresses the news media at her election-night watch party in Hayward, Calif., on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump Officials Impose More Sanctions to Pressure Cuba
item.description: Human rights experts have said that the U.S. attempts to squeeze Cuba’s economy, including an oil blockade, have caused a severe humanitarian crisis.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: Activity in Havana, once bustling, has dwindled as uncertainty grows about the city’s future. Cuba’s economy has suffered because of the U.S. blockade on oil shipments.

item.title: A Man in a Chucky-Style Mask Was Scaring Philadelphians. Then He Picked the Wrong Woman.
item.description: When Jameka Wilson encountered a man wearing a Chucky-style Halloween mask, her stage combat training kicked in. Now she’s a minor local celebrity.
item.dc:creator: Sopan Deb
item.media:description: A masked man was harassing people in Philadelphia early last week. The police are searching for him.

item.title: Duffels Full of Khat Seized at Baltimore Airport’s Baggage Claim
item.description: While Customs and Border Protection said it intercepted more than half a ton of the controlled substance, experts say far more of the East African plant makes it into the country.

item.title: Targeted by an Islamophobic Provocateur, a City’s Muslims Are on Edge

item.title: Homeland Security Made a Big Claim About Noncitizen Voting. Now It Can’t Prove It.
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security told Nevada election officials that it identified 185 “potential” noncitizens on the state’s voter rolls, not the nearly 16,000 it claimed last month.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti
item.media:credit: Roger Kisby for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nevada election officials have questioned the Trump administration’s claims that thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote in the state. Above, a poll worker stands in a polling location in Las Vegas during the state’s primary in June.

item.title: Darline Graham’s Debate Misstep Tests South Carolina’s Appetite for a Political Newcomer
item.description: The South Carolina senator has argued that her lack of political experience is a strength as she runs to succeed her late brother, Lindsey Graham. But a debate misstep has rattled some of her supporters.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham is campaigning to hold on to the seat of her late brother, Lindsey Graham.

item.title: Trump Officials Move to Fund Gaza Peacekeepers Even as Peace Plan Falters

item.title: Massachusetts Police Search for Karen Solomon in Connection to Husband’s Death
